Study and Stay Level 3 — Express Entry Points: Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS)

UBC Okanagan Events

Planning to stay in Canada after graduation? Our Study and Stay Permanent Residence workshops are designed to help you navigate the immigration pathways, policies, and processes you’ll encounter when applying for Permanent Residence. Boise State University Events

Mission V.I.B.E.S.: The process of sending a science payload to space Aged individuals and astronauts experience bone loss despite rigorous physical activity. Bone mechanoresponse is partly regulated by mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) that respond to mechanical challenges. To investigate if microgravity affects the mechanoresponse of MSCs in bone, we developed 3D Bone Marrow Analogs (BMAs) to be maintained in hardware aboard the International Space Station (ISS). To create a BMA model, we generated two idealized 3D trabecular lattices mimicking young (25%) or old (13%) trabecular bone volumes and filled them with hydrogel-encapsulated primary bone marrow MSCs to mimic bone marrow. announcedEngineering & Science

Integrative Biology Seminar - Lillian Aoki, Assistant Professor

Oregon State University Events

Structure, function, and extreme events in coastal vegetated habitats Lillian Aoki is a coastal scientist studying ecosystem dynamics and resilience in nearshore and estuarine habitats. She uses a variety of field, lab, and computational methods to build an integrated and cross-scale understanding of coastal ecology in a rapidly changing world. Current projects focus on understanding recovery trajectories of seagrass meadows following marine heatwaves and the role of land management in facilitating carbon sequestration in tidal marshes. She earned her PhD in Environmental Sciences from the University of Virginia. For more information about Lilian, please go to https://coasts.uoregon.edu/peop

Ten for Teaching: Instituting flexible course policies that support all learners (ASYNCHRONOUS)

Boise State University Events

During the COVID-19 pandemic many educators loosened their course policies (e.g., around attendance and late work). Several years later, some of that flexibility has remained, with educators noting both positive and negative impacts on student learning. This dichotomy leads many of us to wonder what the right balance of flexibility is. In this workshop, we will begin by exploring the demographics of Boise State students and how those might impact the choices we make. In addition, you will have the opportunity to discuss your thoughts and assumptions about course policies, review different policy models, and consider what policies best support your students' learning.
